concerns.text: The plan proposes using a 'KS-test Proxy' dataset (generic parquet) with synthetic labels to validate the statistical pipeline. This fails construct validity: the proxy data does not measure the 'structural precursors' ($D^2_{min}$) or 'shear bands' defined in the spec. Validating a KS-test on random numbers does not validate the ability to detect physical yielding signatures. The methodology cannot answer the research question without the actual MD trajectory data.

The plan acknowledges that KS-test is invalid for clustered data (spatial autocorrelation) and proposes a 'Permutation Test' as a correction, yet the implementation plan (and Spec FR-003) mandates a standard KS-test. Proceeding with a standard KS-test on aggregated data without the permutation correction (or a formal spec amendment) risks Type I errors, invalidating the causal/associational claims regarding brittle vs. ductile regimes.

The plan states: 'If no open MD trajectory dataset exists... the implementation will use the provided KS-test data as a proxy... explicitly flagging the dataset mismatch.' This is a fatal methodological flaw for a scientific claim. A proxy dataset cannot validate the detection of physical phenomena (phase transitions). The research question is unanswerable with the proposed data strategy; the plan must either secure the specific MD data or reframe the project as a 'pipeline validation' only, dropping claims about physical precursors.
